questions.prompt: What is the standard unit for measuring mass in the metric system?

choices.feedback: Litres measure capacity, not mass.
Metres measure length, not mass.
cm² is a unit of area, not mass.

hints: Mass measures how heavy an object is.
The standard metric unit is grams (g).
Think: a paperclip weighs about 1 g.
questions.explanation: The standard metric unit of mass is the gram (g).

questions.prompt: How many grams are in 1 kilogram?

choices.feedback: 100 g = 0.1 kg. There are 1000 g in 1 kg.
10 g = 0.01 kg. There are 1000 g in 1 kg.
10 000 g = 10 kg. There are 1000 g in 1 kg.

hints: The prefix 'kilo-' means one thousand (1000).
Think: a litre of water weighs about 1 kg.

questions.prompt: Why is the kilogram used to measure heavy objects (e.g., a bag of sugar)?

choices.text: Kilograms are larger units, so they give smaller, easier-to-read numbers
Kilograms are more precise than grams
choices.feedback: Kilograms are LESS precise. Grams give more detail.

choices.text: Kilograms are the only units available
choices.feedback: Grams are also available; the choice depends on the object's mass.
No such rule exists. It is a matter of practicality.

hints: A bag of sugar weighs about 1 kg.

When a number has fewer digits, it is usually easier to work with.

questions.prompt: A 2 kg bag of flour is how many grams?

choices.feedback: 2 kg = 2000 g, not 2 g.

questions.prompt: A packet of sugar weighs 500 g. What is its mass in kilograms?

choices.feedback: 500 g = 0.5 kg. 5 kg would be 5000 g.
500 g = 0.5 kg. 50 kg would be 50 000 g.
500 g = 0.5 kg, not 500 kg.

hints: So to convert g to kg, divide by 1000.

questions.prompt: Three packets of flour weigh 1 kg, 2 kg, and 1.5 kg. What is their total mass in grams?
hints: First add the masses in kg: 1 + 2 + 1.5 = 4.5 kg.
Then convert to grams: 4.5 × 1000 = 4500 g.
Or convert each to grams first: 1000 + 2000 + 1500 = 4500 g.

3 kg + 2.5 kg = 5.5 kg, not 550 g.
